decision.rule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
decision.recommendation: DO-NOT-SEAL. Do not record as-is. Every content check passes and the harness object must be kept exactly as it is — it is byte-equal to the accepted parent's DR-G01 entry, and the D-006 unit handling inside it is the strongest thing here and should survive any repair verbatim. The repair is to the authorityClaim only: state the artifact's real reason for existing, and disclose v1. A v4 that either explains what v3 adds over v1 — the parent-review pin and the v2 lineage record — or explains why v1 is superseded despite occupying the promised path, would on these bytes carry no remaining finding known to this reviewer.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: The central attack fails cleanly: the harness object is EQUAL to the live parent's DR-G01 entry, tested by object equality rather than by reading, and all three cited digests verify including the parent-review digest, which points at my own parent verdict and which I recomputed from disk rather than assumed. The D-006 trap is also fully avoided, and avoided well. The bare-integer set is 0, 1, 3, 25 and 26214400; MiB, 1024 and 1048576 all return zero; and both 26214400 occurrences are negations inherited verbatim from the accepted parent, which carries the same two in the same entry. Positively, the artifact holds the unit open — 'the D-006 numeral 25 MB with unit standing UNDECIDED' — and splits the scoring so that size comparison waits for a D-006 unit successor while exclusion membership is scored now. That is the right response to an undecided unit, and it matches my earlier repo-wide finding that no MB-to-bytes definition exists anywhere in COORD or docs/v2/architecture. The finding is not about content. authorityClaim says 'This file exists so the D-086 promised artifactPathWhenAuthored is occupied against the accepted parent.' I resolved that path rather than reading past it. It is harness.DR-G01.core-download.v1.json — and that file exists, pins the accepted parent at 175723e3, and carries a harness object equal to the parent's entry. A key-by-key comparison shows v1 and v3 are substantively identical: harness, parent, parentSha256, registerRow, status, binds, documentClass and date all IDENTICAL, with only artifact, version, the reworded authorityClaim, and v3's two added provenance fields differing. So the claim is false under both readings — v3 is not at the promised path and cannot occupy it, and the condition already held before v3 was written. What compounds it is the predecessor record: predecessorV2 accurately explains that v2 had the right harness but pinned CGHS v2, which I verified at 11a305c6, but the artifact is silent about v1, which has no deficiency and sits at the promised path. Naming only the deficient predecessor is what makes the rationale read as sound. The practical consequence is that three files now carry an identical DR-G01 harness object, two of them pin the accepted parent, and the parent's own pointer names v1 — so 'the DR-G01 extraction' is now ambiguous, which is the exact ambiguity the artifactPathWhenAuthored promise exists to prevent. It is a SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker because nothing prohibited is authored, no gate standing is claimed, nothing is bound, and the extraction itself is exact. Two things to note beyond the finding. Codex is usage-limited per the dispatch; I have named the Codex path, no Codex file exists, and I neither read nor authored one, so this is a single independent review. And neither v1 nor v2 has a verdict of any kind — the same pattern as FX-7 v1, FX-8 v1 and FX-10 v1 this session — which matters here because the defective authorityClaim sentence is also present in v1, so it has gone unreviewed in this chain from the start. Fourteen attacks run, thirteen refuted, one landing.
